sections.h2: What are the main ways to sell a house in O'Fallon, Illinois?
sections.html:
Homeowners in O'Fallon can hire an agent, sell on their own, or take a direct offer from a buyer who pays cash. The right pick turns on the house's condition, the lender's timeline and how much repair work the owner is willing to manage.

This O'Fallon sits in St. Clair County, east of St. Louis, and should not be mixed up with the O'Fallon in St. Charles County, Missouri. Both belong to the St. Louis metro area, which makes the pair unusual. The 2020 census counted 32,289 residents here, and the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 32,656.

  • A listing makes sense for a house that is move-in ready and in a subdivision where comparable sales are easy to find.
  • A sale by owner works when you have the time to show the house and handle paperwork with a title company.
  • A cash purchase works for a house that needs work, a rental with a tenant, or an inherited property. Ask for the offer in writing and weigh it against a listing price minus commission and repairs.

sections.h2: How did O'Fallon grow, and what does that mean for the houses?
sections.html:
O'Fallon began as a railroad town in 1854, and suburban growth picked up in the 1980s and again after Interstate 64 was widened in the 1990s, so a large share of the housing is in subdivisions from those decades. Lots were platted around a Baltimore and Ohio depot and sold at public auction on May 18, 1854, and German settlers came for the farmland.

The village was incorporated on January 27, 1874, and residents voted on March 14, 1905 to switch to a city form of government. Population rose from 7,268 in 1970 to 12,173 in 1980, 21,910 in 2000 and 32,289 in 2020. Subdivision names that come up in listings include Thornbury Hill, Nolin Creek Estates, Fairwood Hills, Deer Creek, Forest Hills and Fairwood East.

The city seal carries a pick and shovel for the coal mines that mattered to the local economy for more than a century, a locomotive for the railroad, and planes for Scott Air Force Base.

sections.h2: Where is O'Fallon, and why does Scott Air Force Base matter to sellers?
sections.html:
O'Fallon is about 5 miles from Scott Air Force Base and roughly 17 miles from downtown St. Louis, which puts a major employer within a short drive. The city center is around two miles east of where Interstate 64 meets U.S. Route 50.

The city flag credits the base as a workplace for many residents, both military and civil service. Sellers who deal with a buyer moving on orders should keep repair receipts, appliance manuals and a recent utility history ready. The Census Bureau lists 4,679 veterans in O'Fallon for 2020-2024.

McKendree University is about 10 miles away. The city covers 15.56 square miles of land (2020), with a density near 2,075 people per square mile.

sections.h2: Which school districts cover O'Fallon homes?
sections.html:
Three districts overlap in O'Fallon: Community Consolidated School District 90, Central School District 104 and O'Fallon Township High School District 203. Buyers often ask for the district first, so print the correct one on your listing sheet.

District 90 runs five elementary schools named Delores Moye, Estelle Kampmeyer, J. E. Hinchcliffe Sr., Laverna Evans and Marie Schaefer, and two junior highs, Amelia V. Carriel and Edward A. Fulton. The high school is O'Fallon Township High School, whose main campus is on South Smiley Street and which has a separate freshman campus called Milburn. Private options include Discovery School, St. Clare Catholic School and First Baptist Academy.

sections.h2: Does O'Fallon require an occupancy permit when a house changes hands?
sections.html:
Yes. The city requires an occupancy permit when the ownership or occupancy of a home changes and no current permit is on file, and a residential permit costs $75 as of May 1, 2025 and stays valid for two years.

The city treats the permit as a property maintenance inspection. After you apply, the schedule runs like this:

  • Contact the city within 7 days of applying to set the inspection appointment.
  • The inspection has to happen within 30 days of the application date.
  • Violations found must be corrected, and the permit is issued within 30 days of that first inspection.
  • Water and electricity must be on during the inspection.

The house may be occupied before the inspection as long as no life safety problems exist. Ameren Illinois and the city's utility billing office ask for the occupancy permit number before they open service. The city offers a seller's and a buyer's "as is" letter, and you should ask your lender whether the permit is a condition of closing. Applications can be made online, at the Community Development Department on the second floor of City Hall, by mail, or through the drop box in the parking lot. Card payments carry a 2.35% convenience fee. Landlords are also pointed to the city's Crime-Free Rental Housing Program.

sections.h2: How do I stop or transfer water service in O'Fallon?
sections.html:
Fill out the city's start or stop service request form, and call Utility Billing at 618-624-4500 extension 1 if you need help. The office is at 255 S Lincoln Avenue and is open Monday through Friday from 7 a.m. to 5:15 p.m.

The city bills water and sewer for most O'Fallon addresses and for most of Fairview Heights. A new account is charged a $50 non-refundable new service fee on its first bill. Sewer charges follow an averaging rule: June, July and August sewer use is billed from the average of the October through April water consumption, with 10,000 gallons assumed for a new residence that has no history. A bill that looks too high can mean a leak, and the city will re-read a meter and run a leak check on request.

sections.h2: When are St. Clair County property taxes due?
sections.html:
St. Clair County bills in two installments, and the bills payable in 2026 were due July 1 and September 1. The Treasurer's calendar for 2026 mailed bills on May 26, set September 18 as the last day to avoid newspaper publication, set October 30 as the last day to pay, and held the tax sale on November 2, 2026, so those dates have passed.

The Treasurer's office keeps hours from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and labels its posted dates tentative until further notice. Ask the Treasurer for the schedule that applies to the next bill, and ask your closing agent whether the seller's share of the current year's tax is credited to the buyer at closing.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers show for O'Fallon?
sections.html:
The numbers describe a family-oriented, owner-heavy city, with 70.2% of housing units owner occupied and 26.2% of residents under 18.

faqs.q: Do I need an occupancy permit to sell my O'Fallon house?
faqs.a: Usually yes, because the city requires one when ownership changes and no current permit is on file. A residential permit costs $75 and lasts two years, and your lender can tell you if closing depends on it.

faqs.q: How long does the O'Fallon occupancy inspection take to schedule?
faqs.a: Contact the city within 7 days of applying, and the inspection must occur within 30 days of the application. The permit itself must be obtained within 30 days after the first inspection.

faqs.q: Can a buyer move in before the occupancy inspection is done?
faqs.a: Yes, provided there are no life safety issues. The city allows occupancy ahead of the inspection, but the inspection still has to happen and any violations still have to be corrected.

faqs.q: Which county collects property tax on an O'Fallon house?
faqs.a: St. Clair County. The Treasurer bills in two installments, and the bills payable in 2026 were due July 1 and September 1. Call the Treasurer for the schedule on the next bill.

faqs.q: Is O'Fallon, Illinois the same place as O'Fallon, Missouri?
faqs.a: No. They are separate cities in the same metro area. Illinois's O'Fallon is in St. Clair County, with 32,289 residents in the 2020 census, so make sure any records or tax searches use the Illinois city.
